# FLX-3403: the related tables cannot be generated as declared

**Family:** seam/conformance (the 3000 band)

FLUX generates the exposes of one contract together: every key the contract declares is laid out from the row index and never repeats, and every foreign key takes a key its parent's rows hold. A relationship whose target the Simulation does not generate from statistics, a key whose declared range or bins hold fewer values than its rows, a one_to_one child with more rows than its parent, a nullFraction on a key column or on a relationship whose joinType is inner, a key declared with a draw that would repeat values, column types that differ between a foreign key and its target, a key column nothing produces, and two relationships that set one column without one implying the other are refused before any row is drawn. So are the declarations that shape how children are placed: a counts entry whose minChildren the child rows or the shape cannot meet, whose parentWhen leaves no parent eligible or reads beyond the parent's own row, or sits on a relationship the layout cannot place (a key, a bridge side, an implied or weighted relationship); a required sum, min or max over the children with no ifNone where a parent can have no children, which would leave it NULL; a link condition on an inner relationship, on a key, or on a relationship another one implies; a bridge whose side is named twice, is one_to_one, carries a nullFraction or has more rows than the pairs of its parents; an association whose side is no generated parent, is one_to_one or takes a parentWhen, a given or an expected count, whose emit declares a history, or that holds more distinct rows than the pairs of its parents; and a weight on a relationship that cannot pick parents by one, on a non-numeric parent column, or with negative or all-zero published values. A reference expose is refused when a published cell does not fit its column. The message names the expose, the column or relationship, and the change to make. A history is refused when its emit has no validity window (one natural entity with a start and an end of one DATE or TIMESTAMP type), when its until, openEnd, chain or start bins leave no room inside timeBounds for an entity's versions, when a tracked column is not categorical, names an undeclared level or has no transition row for a level a chain can reach, when a tracked foreign key has a level that is no key its parent holds in the plan (an identifier key holds a level only when its rows fill every identifier of its length in the plan and the level is one, in lower case hex), or when its parent is not a to-one relationship. A history's parent.lifetime is refused when the parent emit declares no lifetimes entry, or declares a history of its own that sets a lifetime column (a validity, tracked, end or rule-set column), which differs between versions; when the parent's lifetime leaves no room for one version of an entity (the message names `history(<emit>).parent.lifetime`, the entities and their lifetimes); or when the rows of the histories that keep to their parent's lifetime still move after one pass for every emit. A history whose plan reads a projection of itself, directly or through other emits, is not generated. An asOf entry is refused when its relationship does not reach the natural entity of an emit that declares a history, its date is not a DATE or TIMESTAMP column, or a rule sets a column the contract requires from a row read as of a date where its entity has no version, which would write NULL. A snapshots, events or periods entry is refused when its of names no emit with a history (or the emit itself), when a column it names is missing from the history's emit or differs in type, when the projected emit has rows of its own, when an events type has no reason text, when a before or after column maps a column the contract requires and the kept ops leave NULL, when a when reads a column the version does not hold, or reads the history's end column where the history does not carry it (a rule, link or the history sets it), or when a periods entry has no grain, no timeBounds, or more periods than a run holds, a `from` before `timeBounds.start`'s day, a `from` or `through` not before `timeBounds.end` or not a `YYYY-MM-DD` text, or a `through` before the `from`. A DATE or TIMESTAMP column of a history's emit is refused when it declares no range or bins, or a range or bins outside timeBounds, as is a relationship whose parent is a periodic emit. A copy through a sharedColumns entry into another relationship's foreign key is refused when the relationship it goes through reaches an emit that declares a history or is projected from one, whose rows hold a version's cells, not the pick the copy follows; the message names both relationships. A column of an events or periods emit drawn given a version's column or a kind's override reads its level, or where none the marginal its parent's weights and table imply, else its own support; one given another cell the entry sets, with allocation exact, or with neither is refused, naming both. A DATE or TIMESTAMP column drawn from declared statistics is refused when its contract's `range` rule holds none of its dates, or would cut the bins of a column another column is drawn given, or is empty; the message names it.
